title: Make AI explain anything simply
learningObjective: How to make difficult topics easier to understand.
tryThis: Explain [topic] like I'm completely new to it. Use one simple analogy and one everyday example.
whyItWorks: Giving AI clearer instructions about your level of knowledge helps it tailor the explanation instead of defaulting to jargon.

title: Plan a study schedule that actually fits your week
learningObjective: How to turn a vague study goal into a concrete plan.
tryThis: I have [exam/topic] in [X days] and about [Y hours] a week free. Break this into a day-by-day study plan with specific tasks.
whyItWorks: AI is good at breaking a big, fuzzy goal into small, scheduled steps once you give it real constraints.

title: Prepare for a job interview
learningObjective: How to rehearse answers to common interview questions.
tryThis: I'm interviewing for [role] at a [type of company]. Ask me 5 common interview questions for this role, one at a time, and give feedback on my answers.
whyItWorks: Practicing out loud with feedback helps more than just reading generic interview tips.

title: Turn a messy to-do list into a real plan
learningObjective: How to prioritize tasks instead of just listing them.
tryThis: Here's my to-do list: [paste it]. Group these into 'urgent', 'important but not urgent', and 'can wait', and suggest what to tackle first.
whyItWorks: AI can spot patterns and dependencies in a list faster than staring at it yourself.

title: Brainstorm past your first five ideas
learningObjective: How to use AI to get unstuck during brainstorming.
tryThis: Give me 10 different directions for [project/idea], including at least 3 that are unusual or unexpected.
whyItWorks: Asking for quantity and variety up front pushes past the obvious first few ideas everyone thinks of.

title: Make an awkward email sound right
learningObjective: How to adjust tone without losing your point.
tryThis: Rewrite this email to sound more [professional/friendly/concise], but keep the same key points: [paste email].
whyItWorks: Specifying the tone you want gives AI a clear target, instead of a vague 'make this better.'

title: Decode a spreadsheet formula you didn't write
learningObjective: How to get a plain-English breakdown of complex formulas.
tryThis: Explain what this formula does, step by step, in plain English: [paste formula].
whyItWorks: Breaking a formula into its logical steps is often clearer than reading the raw syntax.

title: Get a beginner roadmap for a new skill
learningObjective: How to turn 'I want to learn X' into actual first steps.
tryThis: I want to learn [skill] starting from zero. Give me the first 5 things to focus on, in order, and one small practice exercise for each.
whyItWorks: A concrete first-steps list is more actionable than a huge list of everything there is to know.

title: Compare your options side by side
learningObjective: How to lay out a decision clearly instead of going in circles.
tryThis: I'm deciding between [option A] and [option B] for [goal]. List the real trade-offs of each, not just generic pros and cons.
whyItWorks: Asking specifically for trade-offs tied to your actual goal avoids generic, unhelpful lists.

title: Practice a conversation in a new language
learningObjective: How to get low-pressure speaking/writing practice anytime.
tryThis: Let's have a simple conversation in [language] about [everyday topic]. Correct my mistakes gently after each message.
whyItWorks: On-demand, judgment-free practice partners are hard to find otherwise, especially for beginners.

title: Write a prompt that actually gets what you want
learningObjective: What makes one prompt work better than another.
tryThis: Take a request you'd normally type in one vague sentence, and add: the audience, the format you want, and one example of 'good' output. Compare the two results.
whyItWorks: Specifics about audience, format, and examples are usually what separates a mediocre AI answer from a great one.

title: Get the gist of a dense document fast
learningObjective: How to extract the key points from something long and complicated.
tryThis: Summarize this in plain English, then list the 3 most important things I need to know or do: [paste document text].
whyItWorks: Separating 'what it says' from 'what I need to act on' makes dense text far less overwhelming.

title: Quiz yourself on something you just read
learningObjective: How active recall helps ideas actually stick.
tryThis: Ask me 3 questions to test whether I really understood [concept/article], then tell me what I got right or missed.
whyItWorks: Being asked questions forces real recall, which sticks far better than just re-reading something.

title: Structure a presentation from a pile of notes
learningObjective: How to turn scattered notes into a clear narrative.
tryThis: Here are my rough notes for a presentation on [topic]: [paste notes]. Suggest a clear structure with an opening hook, 3 main points, and a closing takeaway.
whyItWorks: AI is good at spotting a logical order in material that feels jumbled to you because you're too close to it.

title: Plan something thoughtful without the decision fatigue
learningObjective: How to use constraints to get genuinely useful suggestions.
tryThis: Suggest 5 ideas for [a gift/an outing/a meal] for someone who likes [specific interests], within a budget of [amount].
whyItWorks: The more specific constraints you give, the less generic and more useful the suggestions become.

title: Find the weak spots in your own writing
learningObjective: How to get specific, actionable feedback instead of vague praise.
tryThis: Read this and tell me the single weakest paragraph and why, plus one concrete way to fix it: [paste writing].
whyItWorks: Asking for ONE specific weak spot avoids a wall of generic feedback that's hard to act on.

title: Build a realistic new habit plan
learningObjective: How to make a new habit specific enough to actually stick.
tryThis: I want to start [habit] but keep failing at it. Ask me about my actual schedule and obstacles, then suggest a realistic version I could stick to for 2 weeks.
whyItWorks: Habits fail most often from being too ambitious — tailoring to your real constraints helps more than generic advice.

title: Rehearse a tricky conversation before you have it
learningObjective: How to think through a hard conversation calmly in advance.
tryThis: Play the role of [person] in a conversation where I need to [bring up a raise / address a conflict / etc.]. React realistically so I can practice.
whyItWorks: Rehearsing out loud, even with an AI, reduces anxiety and helps you find the right words before it matters.

title: Turn scattered research into an outline
learningObjective: How to organize research before you start writing.
tryThis: Here's everything I've found on [topic]: [paste notes/links/quotes]. Organize this into a logical outline with headings.
whyItWorks: Outlining first, separately from writing, usually produces clearer final work than writing and organizing at the same time.

title: Make sense of a confusing chart or dataset
learningObjective: How to pull the actual takeaway out of raw numbers.
tryThis: Here's a chart/table I don't fully understand: [describe or paste it]. What's the single most important trend or takeaway here?
whyItWorks: Asking for the single most important takeaway, rather than 'explain this,' keeps the answer focused and useful.

title: Create your own practice test
learningObjective: How to generate targeted practice material for an exam.
tryThis: Based on these topics I need to study: [list them], write 5 practice questions at a moderate difficulty, with an answer key.
whyItWorks: Practice testing is one of the most effective study techniques, and AI can generate unlimited fresh questions.

title: Pressure-test an idea before committing to it
learningObjective: How to find holes in your own plan before others do.
tryThis: Here's my plan: [describe it]. Play devil's advocate and give me the 3 strongest objections someone might raise.
whyItWorks: It's much easier to fix a weak plan when you find the objections yourself, in private, ahead of time.

title: Translate confusing fine print into plain English
learningObjective: How to understand terms, contracts, or technical text before agreeing to them.
tryThis: Explain what this actually means for me in plain English, and flag anything that seems like it could matter: [paste text].
whyItWorks: Dense legal or technical language is often simpler than it looks once it's restated plainly — just don't skip reading it entirely.

title: Warm up a stuck creative project
learningObjective: How to use AI as a brainstorming partner, not a ghostwriter.
tryThis: I'm stuck on [story/project]. Ask me 5 questions about it that might help me figure out what happens next.
whyItWorks: Being asked good questions often unlocks ideas faster than being handed an answer outright.
